newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Local tranches lead Singapore shares lower.
newsitem.headline: Local tranches lead Singapore shares lower.

text.p: Singapore shares fell on Monday morning following the sharp drop on Wall Street on Friday, with the local tranches of blue chip stock s leading the way.

Dealers said announcements by several banks on Friday that they had no intention of merging foreign and local tranches for now depressed local tranches of banks like OCBC, UOB, DBS and OUB, but boosted their foreign tranches.

At 0200 GMT, Singapore Press Foreign was Singapore $1.30 up at S$23.30 while its local tranche shed S$0.70 to S$14.20. UOB foreign rose S$1.00 to S$13.30 while its local tranche fell S$0.55 to S$9.05.
Dealers said there was little panic selling despite Wall Street's second biggest one day fall since the October 1987 crash.
"So far, it's just wait and see. Sentiment has become more jittery with Wall Street and the regional currency problems," said a dealer with a local institution.
The Straits Times Industrials Index fell 31.42 points or 11.61 percent to 1,922.38. Volume was moderately light, around 56 million shares, with 19 gainers to 231 losers.
